meta.title: Devrem — A modern electronic circuit simulator
meta.description: Draw your circuit, run it, watch the current flow. A fast, dark-themed electronic circuit simulator for Windows.

hero.title: Draw your circuit, run it,
hero.subtitle: Devrem is a fast, modern electronic circuit simulator written in Rust that simulates analog and digital circuits in real time.

features.title: Your lab bench, on your screen
features.subtitle: Tools that make building and understanding circuits easier, from students to engineers.

items.title: Real-time simulation
items.text: Change a value and see the result instantly. Wires are colored by voltage and current flows as moving dots.

items.title: Analog and digital together
items.text: Transistors, op-amps and the 555 work alongside logic gates, flip-flops and 7-segment displays in one circuit.

items.title: Oscilloscope and Bode plots
items.text: Watch meters live, get the frequency response with AC analysis and characteristic curves with DC sweeps.

items.title: An engine written in Rust
items.text: An MNA-based simulation engine with a Newton-Raphson solver, tested against analytic solutions.

items.title: An easy schematic editor
items.text: Drag and drop, wires from any pin, smart connections, undo / redo and SI-prefixed values (4k7, 100n).

items.title: Export and share
items.text: Save circuits as .dvrm; export SPICE netlists, PNG, SVG and CSV.

showcase.scopeText: Input and output of an inverting op-amp amplifier on the same screen.
showcase.digitalText: A hex counter with a clock, flip-flops, a decoder and a 7-segment display.
showcase.acText: Bode plot of an RC low-pass filter: −3 dB at 1 kHz.

cta.title: Build your first circuit in minutes
cta.text: Devrem is free and needs no account. Build it from source, open a circuit from the example gallery and press F5.

download.title: Install Devrem
download.subtitle: Version {{version}} · Windows 10 / 11 (64-bit)
download.notice: No prebuilt installer is published at the moment. You install Devrem by building it from source yourself. The first setup takes about 20–30 minutes.
tools: Select the "Desktop development with C++" workload.
Run rustup-init.exe and choose the default installation (1).
Download the LTS version (20 or later).
Run it in a new terminal after installing Node.js.
download.runTitle: 3. Run it or build an installer
download.runText: "pnpm dev" opens the app right away. "pnpm build" creates an installer: target\release\bundle\nsis\Devrem_{{version}}_x64-setup.exe — double-click it to install.
requirements: 5–10 GB of free disk space for the build

docs.title: Documentation
docs.subtitle: Everything you need to get started with Devrem.

sections.title: 1. Placing components
body: Pick a component from the list on the left and click the canvas, or drag and drop it. While placing, press R to rotate and Esc to stop.
Select a component to change its values in the Properties panel on the right.

sections.title: 2. Drawing wires
body: Click a pin, click to add corners; the wire finishes automatically when you click another pin, a wire end or a wire.
You can also drag from pin to pin. Press W to start a wire at the cursor.

sections.title: 3. Simulation
body: Press F5 to start the real-time simulation. Wires are colored by voltage: red is high, gray is ground, blue is negative.
While it runs you can click switches, push buttons and logic inputs or drag a potentiometer; the circuit state is kept.
The speed selector sets how much simulated time passes per second of real time. Slow it down to watch fast signals.

sections.title: 4. Analyses
body: The Oscilloscope in the bottom panel plots voltmeter / ammeter / logic probe readings live.
AC Analysis uses the first AC source as the stimulus and produces a Bode plot. DC Sweep sweeps a selected DC source.
Every analysis can be exported as CSV.

sections.title: 5. Writing values
body: Values use SI prefixes: 4k7 = 4.7 kΩ; 100n = 100 nF; 2.2µ or 2.2u = 2.2 µ; 1M = 1 mega; 1m = 1 milli.
